name: Chungsoon Kwak
bio: Chungsoon Kwak was a Korean-American who fought deportation to South Korea, where she feared death under the Syngman Rhee regime. She won a stay of deportation in 1954.
charges: Faced deportation to South Korea under U.S. immigration law, despite fears for her life under the Syngman Rhee regime.

name: Choon Cha Kwak
bio: Choon Cha Kwak was a Korean-American who faced deportation to South Korea in the same case as her husband. The proceedings sought to send the couple back despite their fears under the Syngman Rhee regime.
charges: Faced deportation to South Korea under U.S. immigration law as part of her family's case.

name: Carlos Soule Echeverria
bio: Carlos Soule Echeverria was a Spanish Loyalist volunteer arrested for deportation to Franco's Spain and held at Ellis Island. He was saved by a writ of habeas corpus in May 1954 and allowed to go to Mexico.
charges: Faced deportation to Franco's Spain as an anti-fascist Spanish Loyalist volunteer; held at Ellis Island.

name: Norbert Galvan
bio: Norbert Galvan faced deportation under the Walter-McCarran Act for past Communist Party membership. The Supreme Court upheld the deportation order against him.
charges: Faced deportation under the Walter-McCarran Act for past Communist Party membership.

name: Manuel Cuevas Diaz
bio: Manuel Cuevas Diaz was an anti-Franco Spanish Republican veteran held since 1952 for deportation. His deportation was enjoined in December 1953, and he was allowed voluntary departure to Guatemala.
charges: Faced deportation as an anti-fascist Spanish Republican veteran; held since 1952.

name: Jacob Burck
bio: Jacob Burck was a Pulitzer Prize-winning newspaper cartoonist in Chicago who faced deportation on contradicted informer testimony. The case sought to deport him over alleged Communist affiliation.
charges: Faced deportation under the Walter-McCarran Act on contradicted informer testimony alleging Communist affiliation.

name: Taras Bojarchuk
bio: Taras Bojarchuk was an ex-merchant-marine officer jailed for deportation over alleged Communist Party membership in the 1930s. He was held at Ellis Island and on West Street before being released on bail in December 1954.
charges: Faced deportation under the Walter-McCarran Act over alleged 1930s Communist Party membership; held at Ellis Island.

name: Leon Callow
bio: Leon Callow was a 38-year U.S. resident and father of nine who faced deportation to Greece for political activity. The proceedings sought to expel him over alleged radical affiliation.
charges: Faced deportation to Greece under the Walter-McCarran Act for political activity, after 38 years' U.S. residence.

name: Joseph Cort
bio: Joseph Cort was a physician and former Communist who faced the doctor draft and loss of his citizenship. Under that pressure he fled to Czechoslovakia in 1954.
charges: Draft-evasion / citizenship-revocation pressure that drove him into exile.

name: David Leff
bio: David Leff was a UNESCO employee whose passport was seized over a U.S. loyalty inquiry. A bench warrant was issued for him after he defied a loyalty-board subpoena.
charges: Bench warrant for defying a loyalty-board subpoena; passport seized.

name: Jeremiah Reeves
bio: Jeremiah Reeves was a Black teenager convicted by an all-white Alabama jury and sentenced to death for the alleged rape of a white woman, on a confession he said was coerced. He was held at Kilby Prison while the NAACP took his appeal to the Supreme Court.
charges: Rape (alleged) — a capital conviction on a coerced confession before an all-white jury.

name: Concepcion Estrada Correa
bio: Concepcion Estrada Correa was a 17-year-old Puerto Rican convicted of felony murder by a 'blue-ribbon' jury in New York and sentenced to death. His defenders called the case an ethnic frame-up amid anti-Puerto-Rican hysteria.
charges: Felony murder — a death sentence his defenders called an ethnic frame-up by a biased jury.
convicted: Convicted April 1954; death sentence (stayed pending appeal).

name: Pedro Antonio Rios
bio: Pedro Antonio Rios was a 22-year-old Puerto Rican convicted of felony murder and sentenced to death in New York in the same wave of cases. His defenders called the prosecution an ethnic frame-up.
charges: Felony murder — death sentence (alleged ethnic frame-up).

name: Henry Matthews
bio: Henry Matthews, who used the alias Massio, was a 17-year-old convicted of felony murder and sentenced to death in New York in the same wave of cases. His defenders called the prosecution a frame-up amid anti-Puerto-Rican hysteria.
charges: Felony murder — death sentence (alleged frame-up amid anti-Puerto-Rican hysteria).

name: Paul Freeman
bio: Paul Freeman was a Black man convicted of murder in New York City. His defenders said the conviction rested on a confession extracted by torture.
charges: Murder — a conviction on an allegedly tortured confession.

name: Paul Pfeffer
bio: Paul Pfeffer was convicted of murder in New York City and sentenced to 20 years. His defenders said the conviction rested on an allegedly forced confession.
charges: Murder — on an allegedly forced confession.

name: John Roche
bio: John Roche was convicted of murder in New York City. His defenders said the conviction rested on a confession coerced by police torture.
charges: Murder — on a police-coerced confession.

name: Norman Roye
bio: Norman Roye was a Black man with a New York murder conviction that his defenders repudiated as resting on a forced confession. The case was challenged on that ground.
charges: Murder — a conviction repudiated as based on a forced confession.

name: Jackson Ingram
bio: Jackson Ingram was a Black Georgian jailed in what his defenders called a racial frame-up on theft and false-imprisonment charges. He was sentenced to about ten years.
charges: Theft / false imprisonment — a racial frame-up.

name: Irving Peress
bio: Irving Peress was an Army dentist at the center of Senator Joseph McCarthy's 'Who promoted Peress?' furor in 1954. He was honorably discharged after invoking the Fifth Amendment on a loyalty form.
charges: Penalized under the Doctor Draft Law for invoking the Fifth Amendment on a loyalty form.
convicted: Honorably discharged after invoking the Fifth Amendment.

name: Stanley Orloff
bio: Stanley Orloff was an Army doctor denied a commission after invoking the Fifth Amendment on a loyalty form. He was among the physicians penalized under the Doctor Draft Law in 1954.
charges: Penalized under the Doctor Draft Law for invoking the Fifth Amendment on a loyalty form.

name: Eugene Levin
bio: Eugene Levin was an Army doctor honorably discharged in June 1954 after invoking the Fifth Amendment on a loyalty form. He was among the physicians penalized under the Doctor Draft Law.
charges: Penalized under the Doctor Draft Law for invoking the Fifth Amendment on a loyalty form.

name: Wagner Bridger
bio: Wagner Bridger was an Army doctor given an undesirable discharge after invoking the Fifth Amendment on a loyalty form. He was among the physicians penalized under the Doctor Draft Law in 1954.
charges: Penalized under the Doctor Draft Law for invoking the Fifth Amendment on a loyalty form.

name: Herbert Nelson
bio: Herbert Nelson was denied an Army commission over his 1940 Communist Party membership. He was vindicated by a Circuit Court in February 1954.
charges: Penalized under the Doctor Draft Law for invoking the Fifth Amendment on a loyalty form.
convicted: Denied commission; later vindicated on appeal.
